_comment: Every test the repository deliberately does not run by default, plus tests reported flaky but still running. Validated by scripts/check_flaky_register.py: the ignored set is derived from source, so adding `#[ignore]` without declaring it here fails the gate. An ignored test is a test whose result nobody has; the register exists so that is a stated decision with a reason, not a quiet absence.
policy: A test may be quarantined (ignored) only with (a) a reason naming the external dependency or defect, (b) an entry here, and (c) a note saying what would un-quarantine it. A test reported flaky but not quarantined stays in the default run and is listed under reported_but_not_quarantined so that 'it fails sometimes' is visible rather than folklore.

quarantined.reason: requires running Ollama instance with llama3 model
quarantined.unquarantine_when: a deterministic provider double replaces the live Ollama call, or the suite gains a self-hosted Ollama service in CI

quarantined.reason: makes real provider calls; run explicitly with --ignored
quarantined.unquarantine_when: never by default: a live provider call spends the owner's key and is not reproducible across machines

quarantined.reason: genuine network call; requires a live N-ATLAS endpoint in NATLAS_* env vars
quarantined.unquarantine_when: CI provides a live N-ATLAS endpoint in the environment

quarantined.reason: genuine network call; requires a live N-ATLAS endpoint in NATLAS_* env vars
quarantined.unquarantine_when: CI provides a live N-ATLAS endpoint in the environment

reported_but_not_quarantined.observation: Reported as intermittently failing on Windows in local runs before 2026-11-18. It is NOT ignored: it stays in the default suite and is listed here so a maintainer seeing it fail knows the history without needing to find this file the hard way.
reported_but_not_quarantined.verified: not reproduced in this pass; the entry is a report, not a measurement
